problem.title: Design a Multi-Tenant LLM Inference Router with Zero-Copy RadixAttention Prefix Caching
problem.prompt: Design a multi-tenant LLM inference routing and serving architecture across 64 H100 GPUs handling 2,000 req/sec where 80% of requests carry 4K–16K token system prompts + RAG context, targeting < 250 ms p99 TTFT, > 85% prefix cache hit rate, strict tenant isolation, and graceful degradation under GPU pod overload.

spark.summary: Route requests via a Prefix-Aware Consistent-Hash Router keyed by `(tenant_id, prefix_block_hash)` to GPU Worker Pods running local RadixAttention + CPU-DRAM L2 KV offload.
spark.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, random or round-robin load balancing destroys prefix cache hit rates across 64 GPUs; prefix-aware consistent hashing with bounded-load fallback preserves > 85% hit rates while preventing single-GPU hot spots.
spark.byteSummary:
Even with RadixAttention enabled inside every GPU worker pod, standard round-robin load balancing across 64 H100s drops prefix cache hit rates to ~1/64 (1.5%), forcing every pod to redundantly prefill the same 8K-token system prompts.

A Prefix-Aware Router solves this by hashing the leading prefix blocks (e.g., first 512 tokens salted with `tenant_id`) onto a consistent-hash ring with **bounded load** (Consistent Hashing with Bounded Loads, max 1.25x average queue depth). Requests for the same tenant and system prompt consistently land on the same GPU worker, hitting its local Radix Tree in GPU HBM—or its CPU-DRAM L2 KV cache.

If a celebrity tenant saturates its primary GPU pod beyond the bounded-load threshold, the router spills overflow requests to the next healthy replica on the ring (cold-prefill fallback) rather than letting TTFT spike past 250 ms.

learningJourney.title: Why Prefix Caching Is Mandatory at 2,000 Req/Sec
learningJourney.purpose: Quantify why 2,000 req/sec on a 70B model requires RadixAttention prefix sharing to fit 8K-token prefixes in HBM.

explanation.foundation: Assume a 70B-parameter model (GQA, ~320 KB KV/token in FP16, or ~160 KB in FP8). An 8K-token prefix occupies `8,192 * 160 KB ≈ 1.3 GB` per copy.
explanation.core: With 80% prefix sharing, RadixAttention stores that 1.3 GB **once** per active tenant/prompt instead of duplicating it per concurrent request, freeing 40+ GB HBM per GPU for higher batch sizes and cutting prefill compute by ~85%.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Design a Multi-Tenant LLM Inference Router with Zero-Copy RadixAttention Prefix Caching, watch how why prefix caching is mandatory at 2,000 req/sec interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Production multi-tenant LLM routers pair bounded-load prefix rings with disaggregated Prefill/Decode pods, per-tenant HBM quotas, and RDMA KV transfer.

explanation.foundation: At the API gateway/router, tokenize (or hash normalized UTF-8 chunks) of the leading `K=512` tokens combined with `tenant_id`. Look up the target GPU pod on a consistent-hash ring.

decisionFramework.problem: How to implement Design a Multi-Tenant LLM Inference Router with Zero-Copy RadixAttention Prefix Caching without hitting unbounded tail latency, state divergence, or operational fragility.
decisionFramework.naiveSolution: Use a single unpartitioned path with unbounded retries and synchronous global coordination.
decisionFramework.whyItFails: Global coordination serializes throughput under load, while unbounded retries amplify transient stalls into full outages.
decisionFramework.alternatives: Compare synchronous strict-consistency paths against bounded asynchronous replication, local caching, or partitioned ownership.
decisionFramework.decision: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, random or round-robin load balancing destroys prefix cache hit rates across 64 GPUs; prefix-aware consistent hashing with bounded-load fallback preserves > 85% hit rates while preventing single-GPU hot spots.
decisionFramework.tradeOffs: Gains predictable p99 latency and fault isolation in exchange for explicit bounding, observability, and slightly higher implementation complexity.

learningJourney.title: GPU HBM Radix Tree + Async CPU DRAM L2 Cache
learningJourney.purpose: Tier GPU HBM Radix Trees with async PCIe Gen5 offloading to a 512 GB CPU-DRAM L2 KV cache.

explanation.foundation: Each GPU worker runs a local Radix Tree over PagedAttention blocks. When HBM utilization crosses 85%, leaf nodes with `ref_count == 0` offload asynchronously over PCIe Gen5 (~64 GB/s) to a 512 GB CPU-DRAM L2 pool.
explanation.core: Reloading an 8K prefix (1.3 GB) from CPU DRAM takes ~20 ms—over 10x faster than cold GPU prefill.
explanation.deepDive: In production deployments of Design a Multi-Tenant LLM Inference Router with Zero-Copy RadixAttention Prefix Caching, watch how gpu hbm radix tree + async cpu dram l2 cache interacts with tail latency, retry amplification, and partial failures. Production multi-tenant LLM routers pair bounded-load prefix rings with disaggregated Prefill/Decode pods, per-tenant HBM quotas, and RDMA KV transfer.

sectionDiagram.title: GPU HBM Radix Tree + Async CPU DRAM L2 Cache

cards.label: 85% Watermark
cards.detail: Start background PCIe offloading at 85% HBM so active decodes never stall waiting for free pages.

cards.label: 16-Token Page Granularity
cards.detail: Fixed PagedAttention blocks transfer cleanly over pinned DMA buffers.

cards.label: Leaf-First Eviction
cards.detail: Evict unreferenced leaf suffixes first, keeping shared system-prompt roots in HBM.

learningJourney.title: Integrating RadixAttention with Disaggregated Prefill/Decode Pods
learningJourney.purpose: Disaggregate Prefill and Decode pods so heavy 16K-token prefills never cause inter-token latency spikes on decode.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Integrating RadixAttention with Disaggregated Prefill/Decode Pods** as the intuition layer for Design a Multi-Tenant LLM Inference Router with Zero-Copy RadixAttention Prefix Caching: Disaggregate Prefill and Decode pods so heavy 16K-token prefills never cause inter-token latency spikes on decode.
explanation.core: At 2,000 req/sec, mixing 16K-token prefills with active decode batches causes inter-token latency (ITL) spikes. Route cache misses and partial suffix prefills to dedicated **Prefill Pods** (which own the Radix Tree), then RDMA/NVLink-transfer only the final KV blocks to **Decode Pods** for smooth token streaming.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, integrating radixattention with disaggregated prefill/decode pods becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production multi-tenant LLM routers pair bounded-load prefix rings with disaggregated Prefill/Decode pods, per-tenant HBM quotas, and RDMA KV transfer.

sectionDiagram.title: Integrating RadixAttention with Disaggregated Prefill/Decode Pods

cards.label: Why Disaggregate
cards.detail: A single 16K-token prefill stalls all co-located decode streams for ~250 ms if run on the same GPU.

cards.label: Prefill Owns Radix
cards.detail: Prefill pods maintain the Radix Tree and only transfer the active request's KV blocks to Decode.

cards.label: Independent Scaling
cards.detail: Scale Prefill GPUs for TTFT and Decode GPUs for token throughput independently.

sectionDiagram.summary: Disaggregating Prefill (Radix-owning) and Decode pods over RDMA eliminates prefill-induced decode jitter.
sectionDiagram.caption: Disaggregating Prefill (Radix-owning) and Decode pods over RDMA eliminates prefill-induced decode jitter.

learningJourney.title: Enforcing Tenant Quotas & Zero Cross-Tenant Leakage
learningJourney.purpose: Enforce zero cross-tenant leakage and noisy-neighbor isolation via salted Radix roots and per-tenant HBM quotas.

explanation.foundation: Think of **Enforcing Tenant Quotas & Zero Cross-Tenant Leakage** as the intuition layer for Design a Multi-Tenant LLM Inference Router with Zero-Copy RadixAttention Prefix Caching: Enforce zero cross-tenant leakage and noisy-neighbor isolation via salted Radix roots and per-tenant HBM quotas.
explanation.core: Salt every Radix Tree root with `(tenant_id, model_version, lora_id)` so cross-tenant hits are impossible. Pair global LRU with **per-tenant HBM soft caps** (e.g., max 25% of HBM per tenant) so a single tenant's 16K-token sweep cannot thrash other tenants' warm caches.
explanation.deepDive: Under heavy load or partial failure, enforcing tenant quotas & zero cross-tenant leakage becomes a critical lever for predictable latency and correctness. Production multi-tenant LLM routers pair bounded-load prefix rings with disaggregated Prefill/Decode pods, per-tenant HBM quotas, and RDMA KV transfer.

sectionDiagram.title: Enforcing Tenant Quotas & Zero Cross-Tenant Leakage

cards.label: Side-Channel Closure
cards.detail: Salting every Radix root with tenant_id ensures Tenant B can never probe Tenant A's TTFT.

cards.label: 25% Soft Quota
cards.detail: One tenant flooding 32K-token prompts only evicts its own older leaves once above 25% HBM.

cards.label: LoRA / Version Safety
cards.detail: Including model_version and lora_id prevents corrupt KV reuse across adapter switches.

sectionDiagram.summary: Salted Radix roots and 25% per-tenant HBM caps eliminate timing side channels and noisy-neighbor cache eviction.
sectionDiagram.caption: Salted Radix roots and 25% per-tenant HBM caps eliminate timing side channels and noisy-neighbor cache eviction.

beginner.summary: Send requests with the same tenant and system prompt to the same GPU so it can reuse cached prefix memory instead of recomputing it.
beginner.keyTakeaway: If one GPU gets too busy, spill extra requests to a backup GPU so response times stay fast.
beginner.byteSummary:
Across 64 GPUs, random routing wastes prefix caching because each GPU has to re-read the same system prompt. A smart router hashes the tenant ID and prompt start so matching requests hit the same GPU.

If that GPU gets crowded, overflow traffic routes to a backup GPU.

intermediate.summary: Use a `(tenant_id, prefix_hash)` consistent-hash router with bounded-load spillover, local HBM Radix Trees, and CPU-DRAM L2 KV offload.
intermediate.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, random or round-robin load balancing destroys prefix cache hit rates across 64 GPUs; prefix-aware consistent hashing with bounded-load fallback preserves > 85% hit rates while preventing single-GPU hot spots.
intermediate.byteSummary:
Hashing the salted prefix onto a consistent-hash ring keeps warm prefixes localized on specific H100s. Bounded-load checks (1.25x cap) prevent hot-GPU queuing.

Offloading evicted GPU pages to 512 GB CPU DRAM cuts reload latency 10x compared to cold prefill.

advanced.summary: Production multi-tenant LLM routers pair bounded-load prefix rings with disaggregated Prefill/Decode pods, per-tenant HBM quotas, and RDMA KV transfer.
advanced.keyTakeaway: To keep the architecture evolvable without sacrificing reliability, random or round-robin load balancing destroys prefix cache hit rates across 64 GPUs; prefix-aware consistent hashing with bounded-load fallback preserves > 85% hit rates while preventing single-GPU hot spots.
advanced.byteSummary:
At 2,000 req/sec, isolating prefill bursts from decode streaming requires disaggregated Prefill Pods owning the Radix Tree and transferring KV blocks over RDMA to Decode Pods.

Tenant salting blocks TTFT timing side channels, while per-tenant HBM quotas prevent noisy-neighbor cache thrashing.

prerequisites.title: AI/LLM Prefix Caching & RadixAttention (Zero-Copy KV Sharing)
prerequisites.summary: RadixAttention indexes cached GPU KV-cache blocks in a compressed prefix trie (Radix Tree) with LRU eviction, enabling zero-copy prefix sharing across concurrent and sequential LLM requests.

prerequisites.title: Consistent Hashing & Virtual Nodes
prerequisites.summary: Consistent hashing assigns data keys to servers in a way that limits how many keys move when servers are added or removed. This helps avoid widespread cache misses and sudden load on databases.

prerequisites.title: Disaggregated LLM Serving (Prefill vs. Decode Pools)
prerequisites.summary: Disaggregated LLM serving separates prompt prefill (compute-bound TTFT) and autoregressive token decode (HBM-bandwidth-bound ITL) onto independent GPU pools, transferring computed KV-cache blocks over RDMA or NVLink without stalling in-flight decode batches.
